items.title: 13'' MacBook Pro, 3.1ghz dual-core i7, 16GB of RAM, Intel Iris 5100 (2014)
items.description: Are there newer MBPs? Yes. Do I need one? No. Plus the horrendous butterfly keyboard: Apple is finally killing it, but not yet on the 13''. And I don't consider anything bigger than that.

items.title: Dell Ultrasharp U2415 24''
items.description: Outstanding price-quality ratio. Rotates to vertical. That pays off on code reviews.

items.title: Das Keyboard 4C TKL
items.description: German-made mechanical keyboard, 87-key layout of pure excellence. Cherry MX Blue, for a noisy typing experience. The best wired mechanical keyboard on the market.

items.title: Ergonomic vertical mouse
items.description: All vertical mice are the same. Don't waste money on an expensive one. The accessory worth real money is the keyboard.

items.title: Razer Kiyo camera
items.description: Meets the minimum specs for high-quality streaming: the best out of the cheapest. The ring light and the USB power gave me some trouble. Nothing horrible, a bit cumbersome.

items.title: HyperX Cloud MIX
items.description: Before you judge me: there are as many headsets as people nowadays. It's madness. The Cloud MIX fits my requirements per-fect-ly. One headset for gaming and working. Great for music, great bass, fast Bluetooth. And superior for gaming: they're made for that. Worth every single penny.

items.title: RØDE NT microphone
items.description: It's this one or the Blue Yeti. Both are USB, so no music-nerd setup required. Plug in and enjoy almost-studio quality on your video calls.

items.title: Airpods (1st Gen)
items.description: Bought second hand in 2020. I only need an unobtrusive headset for on-the-go calls. Others sound better. None mic better.

items.title: Cyxus Ayanna glasses
items.description: I wore blue-filter glasses before they were a thing. My first pair were Gunnar Onyx: best brand, expensive as hell. Then I learned how the tech works. Now I don't spend more than 30 bucks, and neither should you.

items.title: Electric sit/stand desk
items.description: For a normal-sized table one motor is enough, and any brand works the same. But buy electric. I had a manual one and you end up never changing modes.

items.title: Interstuhl UPis1 100U
items.description: Hands down, this removes lower back pain. It's a stool with a rounded base, so you stabilize yourself all the time. Height is a non-issue with the desk above.

items.title: Eames plastic chair
items.description: Best chair ever. Worth it for historical reasons alone: this chair changed the world. Read up on Eames design.

items.title: Standing desk mat
items.description: Stand long enough and your feet, hips and knees complain. A desk mat releases that stress. Any brand works.

items.title: VS Code
items.description: I was an Atom fanboy: plug-and-play, unlike Sublime. VS Code is Atom on steroids. It's built on TypeScript, so its TypeScript support is the best in town.

items.title: Hyper
items.description: There are many terminals out there. This one is TypeScript-based.

items.title: Fish shell
items.description: The terminal is nice, but have you ever played with shells? This is the real deal. Fish is out of this world.

items.title: SynthWave '84 theme
items.description: Of course. What did you expect? The freaking best theme EVER, period. It matches my vapor/retro aesthetic.

items.title: Menlo font (Bitstream Vera)
items.description: The monospace font that ships with the MacBook. Always favour the standards. Open-sourcerer? Try Bitstream Vera. Menlo descends from it.

items.title: Brave Browser
items.description: Best UX. And one subtle developer superpower: block your analytics stack and watch your web break. It will. Believe me.

items.title: dotfiles
items.description: All my cool configs. Steal anything you want. My aliases are legendary.

items.title: eqMac equalizer
items.description: How does Apple not include this by default? The missing audio setting. Huge kudos to the maintainers. The bass drops are extra juicy now.

items.title: Dropbox Paper
items.description: Notion is great and has two flaws: my small brain can't handle all the options, and copy-pasting, the 101 of note-taking, is broken. A solid second place. Paper is just perfectly balanced.

items.title: Avast Password
items.description: I know, weird. I don't know anyone else using it. But it covers everything I need for free: multiple devices, cross-platform, notes and cards, top-notch autofill.

items.title: 1clipboard
items.description: I can't live without this. Are you ok sharing your clipboard with Apple? I'm not. Long live the OSS!

items.title: Gifski
items.description: GitHub doesn't allow mp4/avi/mov videos. It can't resize a gif for you either. It's just... I can't. Thanks, Sindre.

items.title: Kap
items.description: Record anything on your screen, outstanding UX. Again: how is this not part of macOS? Again: thank you, Sindre.

items.title: Sketch
items.description: Brilliant piece of software. I found Sketch and designing felt fun again. All my assets are powered by it.
